chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

Al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ passed by a woman at Minā while she was weeping, and her children were around her weeping, and a cow of hers had died. He drew near to her and said to her, "What makes you weep, O maidservant of Allah?" She said, "O servant of Allah, we have orphaned children, and I had a cow from which came my livelihood and the livelihood of my children. It has died, and I have been left cut off, together with my children; we have no means."

He said, "O maidservant of Allah, would you like me to revive it for you?" So she was inspired to say, "Yes, O servant of Allah." Then he withdrew, prayed two rakʿahs of salat (prayer), then raised his hand for a short while and moved his lips. Then he stood and called out at the cow, and prodded it with a prod or struck it with his foot, whereupon it rose upright standing upon the ground.
So when the woman looked at the cow, she cried out and said, "ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah!" Then he mixed among the people, came to be between them, and went on, peace be upon him.

key_terms.أُحْيِيَهَا: That I revive it; bringing the cow back to life by Allah’s leave.
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: A title used here for the righteous servant, referring to the Imam عليه السلام.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Kaʿbah, invoked in the woman’s oath after witnessing the event.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two rakʿahs of salat (prayer) performed before the miracle occurred.
key_terms.مَعِيشَتِي: My livelihood; the source of sustenance for the woman and her children.
key_terms.يَتَامَى: Orphaned children who depended on the woman’s means of livelihood.

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kafi describe Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام reviving a dead cow for a poor woman at Minā?
ai.summary: This narration describes al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام showing compassion to a grieving woman whose family livelihood had been lost with the death of her cow. By Allah’s leave, after salat (prayer) and supplication, he revived the animal, demonstrating a sign associated with his sanctified station and mercy toward the vulnerable.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) passed by a woman at Mina, and she was crying, and her children were crying around her, and a cow of hers had died. So he<sup>asws</sup> went closer to her, then said to her: ‘What makes you cry, O maid of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ She said, ‘O servant of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! For us there are orphaned children, and there was a cow for me for my livelihood and the livelihood of my children which was from it, and it has died, and I and my children have been cut off, there are no means for us’.

So heasws said: ‘O maid of Allahazwj! Would it be a solution for you if Iasws were to revive it for you?’ So she was inspired and said, ‘Yes, O servant of Allahazwj!’. So heasws went aside and prayed two Cycles of Salat, then raised hisasws hands for a while and moved hisasws lips, then stood, so heasws struck the cow and pushed it with a push or struck it with hisasws leg. So it sat upright upon the ground and stood up.

So when the woman looked at the cow, she shouted and said, ‘Isa<sup>as</sup> Bin Maryam<sup>as</sup>, by the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Kabah!’. So he<sup>asws</sup> mingled with the people and came to be between them and went away’.
en.sarwar: The monk then asked him many questions. The Imam (a.s.) answered them all. He asked the monk certain questions which he could not answer but the Imam (a.s.) himself answered them.. The monk then said, “Tell me of the eight letters that were revealed out of which four were manifested on earth and the other four remained in space. To who the four were sent thhe fpur that remained in space? Who will interpret them?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “He will be our al-Qa’im (the one who will rise with Divine authority). Allah will sent them to him and he will interpret them. He will sent to him what has not even been sent to the truthful ones, the messengers and the rightly guided ones.” Then the monk said, “Tell me about the of the four that were sent to earth. What are they?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “I will tell you about all four. The first one was ‘there is no lord except Allah Who is One and has no partners that He is eternal ’. The second was, ‘Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah purely’. The third one was we the Ahl al-Bayt (infallible members of the family of Muhammad (s.a.). the fourth one was our Shi‘a (followers) who are from us and we are from the Messenger of Allah and the Messenger of Allah is from Allah through means.” The monk then said, “I testify that there is no lord except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and that whatever he brought from Allah is true and that your, Ahl al-Bayt (the infallible members of the family of Muhammad (s.a.) are the chosen of Allah from His creatures and that you Shi‘a are pure who are the replacement (of those who oppose you). They will have the good end. All thanks are due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.” Abu Ibrahim (a.s.) called to bring for him a gown, a shirt made in Gha’in Khurasan, a scarf, a shoe and a hat. He gave them to him and prayed the noon time prayer and asked him to circumcise. He said, “ It had been done when he was seven years old.”
